stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours. Pipe B can empty the same tank in 10 hours. If both pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty, how many hours will it take to fill the tank completely?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student adds the rates instead of subtracting: 1/6 + 1/10 = 5/30 + 3/30 = 8/30 = 4/15, giving time = 15/4 which they round to 4.
Student computes net rate = 1/6 - 1/10 = 2/30 correctly but then inverts as 30/2 = 15, and then adds 1 for an off-by-one, giving 16.
Student computes net rate as 1/6 - 1/10 = 1/8 (wrong arithmetic: 10-6=4 over 60, giving 4/60=1/15 but student makes error and gets 1/8), giving 8.
Net fill rate = 1/6 - 1/10 = 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15 tank per hour. Time = 15 hours.

explanation: Pipe A fills at 1/6 tank per hour. Pipe B drains at 1/10 tank per hour. Net rate with both open = 1/6 - 1/10. LCM of 6 and 10 is 30: 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. Time to fill = 1/(1/15) = 15 hours.

explanation_sections.punchline: Net rate = fill rate - drain rate = 1/6 - 1/10 = 1/15 tank/hour, so 15 hours to fill.
explanation_sections.approach: Assign signs: filling pipe contributes positive rate, emptying pipe contributes negative rate. Net rate = 1/6 - 1/10. Use LCM = 30: 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. Time = reciprocal of net rate = 15.
explanation_sections.lesson: Emptying pipes subtract from the combined rate. Never add a drain rate to a fill rate.
explanation_sections.timing: 70-85 seconds. The trap is option 1 (4 hours) from adding rates instead of subtracting.
